title: Jamaican Jerk Chicken with Escovitch, Honey Jerk Sauce and Festival
summary: Leg quarters rubbed with a heavy layer of dried spices and a blended Scotch bonnet, thyme and allspice paste, marinated for a day or two, then grilled and smoked over lump charcoal. Served on fried festival bread with a quick escovitch pickle and a sweet honey jerk sauce, in Irie Jerk Chicken's style.
notes: Video: 'Authentic Jerk Chicken at Home' on the Joshua Weissman Recipes channel (UCUAg71CJEvFdOnujmep1Svw). Guest: Niki Gordon of Irie Jerk Chicken, Brooklyn. Written recipe: https://www.joshuaweissman.com/recipes/authentic-jerk-chicken-at-home (serves 4, prep 30 min, cook 1 hour). Marinating (24 hours minimum, ideally 48) is not in prep_minutes (house rule 13). The video cooks a restaurant-size batch and says the 4-serving amounts are in on-screen notes and the written recipe; the on-screen notes are not in the transcript, so nearly every amount comes from the written recipe. The leg quarters are entered as bought, bone-in (house rule 12): 4 x about 340 g = 1360 g (our estimate; the lead converts to edible weight). Other estimates: 15 g per Scotch bonnet or Jamaican hot pepper, 10 g pimento pepper, 100 g for a bunch of green onions, 200 g festival mix for 4 servings (50 g each), 1/2 cup water for the dough, 1/4 tsp salt in the sauce, 32 g absorbed oil (10% of the raw dough). Proxies: Scotch bonnet for the Jamaican hot pepper; sweet red pepper for the pimento seasoning pepper; the sorrel drink (store-bought ginger-sorrel in the video; the page calls it sorrel tea and gives a homemade version, written up separately as sorrel-drink-joshua-weissman) uses a cranberry juice cocktail proxy; Jamaican chicken seasoning and Sazón use the USDA sazon seasoning mix and dry jerk seasoning uses the USDA chili seasoning mix, so sodium is uncertain. The salt in this recipe comes from those blends (the video says no plain salt is added to the chicken). The thick wet marinade stays on the chicken and is counted in full; the 1/2 cup set aside for the sauce is part of it, and the sauce (spooned over, made for these 4 plates, about 2/3 cup) adds only honey, sorrel and salt, and is counted in full: it is drizzled, not a tossed glaze from a bigger batch (house rules 1 and 10). Nutmeg powder is on the page but not named in the video. Not counted: the vinegar and lime wash (rinsed off), allspice and nutmeg thrown on the coals, the escovitch's whole allspice and its vinegar, and the festival frying oil in the pot. The written recipe adds 1 Tbsp kosher salt to the escovitch, but the video says 'no salt', so it is left out. Festival bread and escovitch are served on the same plate, so they are groups here, not separate recipes.

steps.text: Clean the leg quarters: scrape out the leftover liver and kidney bits from the cavity side, leaving the fat and skin on.
Wash the chicken with the lime juice and vinegar in cold water, rubbing away any remaining bits, then drain well.

Wet marinade: blend the Scotch bonnets, Jamaican and pimento peppers (seeds and all), ginger, thyme, green onions, sorrel drink, whole allspice and sweet onion into a smooth paste. Set aside 1/2 cup for the sauce.

Season the chicken all over with the garlic powder, nutmeg, ground ginger, chicken seasoning, Sazón, jerk seasoning and ground allspice, then pour on the wet paste and massage it in, pushing it under the skin and into any cuts.
Cover and refrigerate at least 24 hours, ideally 48.
Light hardwood lump charcoal (not briquettes), banked in the middle of the grill, and toss some whole allspice berries and whole nutmeg onto the coals for aroma.

Grill the chicken without oil over the coals with the lid closed and a vent open, at around 300°F, about 15 minutes per side, poking it all over with a fork after turning. Once both sides are charred, move it to the top rack for another 15 minutes, until it reaches at least 165°F in the thickest part.

Escovitch: slice the onion into very thin rounds and the peppers into rounds, and cut the carrot into thin pieces. Put them in a pot with the whole allspice, add vinegar just to cover (no salt), bring to a boil over medium-high heat, then turn off the heat.
Sweet honey jerk sauce: blend the reserved marinade with the honey and a splash of sorrel drink on high until smoother, then season with salt to taste.

Festival: mix most of the festival mix with water by hand into a soft dough that is firm but not sticky, adding the rest of the mix if needed. Shape into logs and fry in oil at 350°F until golden, 3-4 minutes. Drain.
Chop each leg quarter into three pieces if you like. Plate the festival bread, add the jerk chicken, a mound of escovitch and spoon the honey jerk sauce over the chicken.
